C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No. 864
Date 26/1/27

January 25th

Sir,
    Certain members of the Boh Ling Tong in this
locality are endeavouring to frame an impeachment
which will be sent to the Central Government against
the Tuchun of Che kiang province, Lu Yung Teh.
He is accused amongst other things of having issued
a licence to a subject of one of the belligerent
nations in order that he might buy arms and
ammunition in Shanghai and transport them to
his own country.
    The Boh Ling Tong are being instigated to act
by persons who are supplying the information on
which the proceedings are being taken.

Your Obedient Servant,

Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

HISI

情报官登记处
第 864 号
日期 27/1/26

1月25日

先生，
    本地保灵堂（Boh Ling Tong）的某些成员正试图构拟一份弹劾书，呈送中央政府，指控浙江省督军卢永祥。除其他事项外，他被指控向某一交战国国民颁发许可证，以便该人能在上海购买军火弹药并运往其本国。
    保灵堂是受那些提供诉讼依据信息的人士唆使而采取行动的。

您顺从的仆人，

总巡捕房督察长。

警务处总监。

HISI

E.H.Murray on the above subject both of which took place on the
premises of the U.S.Court for China, Whangpoo Road, in a room fur-
nished like a bedroom on the third floor ( probably Murray,s
bedroom).

the huchow and was informed that this was necessary as these
documents were not issued to Chinese who were not highly placed
in the Government.    The answer seemed to satisfy Murray who
then explained that the consignment of rifles consisted of
15,000 with 500 rounds of ammunition for each;    That ¼ of the
whole belonged to a German, while ¾ belonged to Chinese;    that
they were on account to be sent for the use of the Russians, and
that they were in a large godown at Pootung, mixed up with other
packages and articles of merchandise and therefor difficult to
sort out.
    Murray was assured that the arms were for the use of
Chinese only and his query as to where they are to be used was
refused an answer.    He then stated terms which were that Tls.
825,000 (the price of the whole consignment and ammunition at
Tls. 55 each) be deposited in the Netherlands Trading Society,
No. 21 The Bund (Yu Ya Ching is compradores to that Bank) and
proof to the effect that this has been done in the shape of a
paper signed by the Manager, be produced by the buyer of the
arms.    Also when the goods are shown a cheque for Tls. 250,000
will be produced by the buyer and perused by the seller before
starting to see the arms.    The Astor House was suggested as

中央巡捕房。
1916年12月22日

关于企图进行武器交易的报告。

由 副巡捕房督察长布鲁斯特（D.S.I. Brewster）制作    转呈者 □□□

先生
    警务线人就上述事宜与 E.H.默里又进行了两次面谈，这两次面谈均发生在黄浦路美国驻华法院（U.S. Court for China）内三楼一间布置如卧室的房间（可能是默里的卧室）。
    默里想知道为何护照上使用了外国人的名字，他被告知这是必要的，因为这些文件不会签发给政府中职位不高的中国人。这个答复似乎令默里满意，他随后解释说，这批步枪共计15,000支，每支配备500发子弹；其中四分之一属于一名德国人，四分之三属于中国人；据称这些武器是供俄国人使用的，它们存放在浦东的一个大仓库里，与其他包裹和商品混杂在一起，因此难以分拣。
    有人向默里保证，这些武器仅供中国人使用，但他询问武器将在何处使用时，未获答复。随后他提出了交易条件，即825,000两白银（整批货物及弹药的价格，按每套55两计算）需存入外滩21号的荷兰银行（Netherlands Trading Society）（虞洽卿是该银行的买办），并由武器买方出具一份由经理签署的文件，以证明此事已办妥。此外，当展示货物时，买方将出示一张250,000两白银的支票，在开始查看武器前由卖方查验。建议将礼查饭店（Astor House）作为

a suitable meeting place. Two men from each side will then
accompany the buyer and seller to examine the arms and if they
are found unsatisfactory the deal is off and the buyer keeps
his cheque. If satisfactory, arrangements will be made for
payment on delivery.
The terms are, as usual, farcical and I have instructed
our agent to point this out to Murray and also to impress upon
him that the principals in the deal are not in Shanghai, that
they have got plenty of money and are willing to pay for
satisfactory goods, that they are waiting a report from their
representative (our agent) here, as to the suitability of the
arms which must be sufficiently up to date to be of use against
soldiers of the Chinese Army and finally that his principals
are not so foolish as to hand a huge sum of money to a comparatively obscure Bank in Shanghai simply for the privilege of
looking at what may turn out to be a lot of useless junk. As
Murray seems to be anxious to make a deal this may bring him
to reason. Results will be reported in due course.
Your obedient servant,
W.B. Alexander /
Detective Sub-Inspector.
Chief Detective Inspector.

合适的会面地点。届时双方各出两人陪同买卖双方查验武器，若发现武器令人不满意，则交易取消，买方保留其支票。若令人满意，则将安排货到付款。
这些条件一如既往地荒谬可笑，我已指示我方线人向默里指出这一点，并向他强调，交易的主要当事人不在上海，他们资金充足，愿意为满意的货物付款，他们正在等待其代表（即我方线人）在此地提交的关于武器适用性的报告，这些武器必须足够新式，以便用于对抗中国军队士兵，最后，其主要当事人并不愚蠢，不会仅仅为了获得查看可能是一堆无用废品的特权，就将巨款交给上海一家相对不知名的银行。鉴于默里似乎急于达成交易，这可能会使他恢复理智。结果将在适当时候报告。
您顺从的仆人，
W.B. 亚历山大 /

REPORT ON Attempt to Trade in Arms.
Made by D.S.I.Brewster. Forwarded by
Sir,
The Police Agent has now had two interviews with a foreigner
re this matter viz Mr. Murray, an employee at the American
Post Office.
Murray accompanied our agent to a restaurant on Nanking
Road about noon on the 19th inst., saw the huchow and professed
himself quite satisfied with it. Another interview has been
arranged for this afternoon when it is hoped that substantial
progress will be made in the negotiations. It will be recollected
that Murray's name has been mentioned before in connection
with trading in arms.
Our Agent has been at considerable trouble and expense in
conducting this affair and I beg to apply that he be rewarded
for his efforts in the matter so far, with, say $10.00.
Your obedient servant,
WBrewster.

先生，
    警务线人就此事宜与一名外国人进行了两次面谈，即默里先生，他是美国邮局的一名雇员。
    本月19日中午左右，默里陪同我方线人前往南京路的一家餐馆，查看了护照，并表示对此完全满意。另一次面谈已安排在今天下午，希望谈判能取得实质性进展。应当记得，默里的名字此前曾与武器交易有关联而被提及。
    我方线人在处理此事上耗费了大量精力和费用，我恳请对他迄今为止的努力给予奖励，例如10.00美元。

先生，
    根据指示，上述案件中的警务线人于本月16日再次前往余杭路4号，并向那里的菲律宾人展示了护照。他被告知第二天去见一位出售武器的外国人。他照做了，并被带到美国驻华法院，在那里他遇到了一位年长的外国人，经过一番交谈后，该外国人告诉我方线人今天中午12点在南京路的一家餐馆与他见面并展示护照，届时将讨论进一步的条件。
您顺从的仆人，
M.布鲁斯特。
副巡捕房督察长。
总巡捕房督察长。

Shanghai Municipal Council.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL POLICE FORCE）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH)

December 15th 1918

Sir,
In connection with the attached the Military
Governor informs me that last summer Barnes Moss
and a Chinese offered to sell him 15000 mauser
rifles and 500,000 cartridges which they said
were stored in some place in Pootung.
They asked $25 for each rifle and $50 for
each 10,000 rounds of ammunition. They demanded
that $50,000 should be advanced as a guarantee
of good faith. The Governor sent this sum to
the City Magistrate with instructions to see
the matter through but he could do nothing as
the arms were never produced.

Your Obedient Servant,

[签名]

Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处）
警务处，
（侦探科）

1918年12月15日

先生，
    关于附件所述事宜，军事总督告知我，去年夏天，巴恩斯·莫斯（Barnes Moss）和一名中国人向他提出出售15,000支毛瑟步枪和500,000发子弹，并称这些武器储存在浦东的某个地方。
    他们要求每支步枪25美元，每10,000发子弹50美元。他们要求预付50,000美元作为诚意保证金。总督将这笔款项交给市公廨裁判官，指示其处理此事，但由于武器从未出示，裁判官无能为力。

您顺从的仆人，

[签名]

总巡捕房督察长。

警务处总监。

pages.en:
Form 2    34
Shanghai Municipal Police.
864
Central    Station.
Novr. 17th    1916.
REPORT ON    attempt to trade in arms.
Made by    D.S.I. Brewster    Forwarded by
Sir,
Fong Wei Ching 馮煥卿 again interviewed does not so far,
modify his terms to any appreciable extent. He seems to be
inclined to make a deal however and now proposes that the
buyer of the arms, who must be prepared to buy the whole lot,
bring to his house, with an escort of 20 armed men if necessary,
the sum of $600,000 in cash which is half the price of the
consignment of 20,000 rifles with 500 rounds for each.
If he is satisfied that the notes are genuine he will return
them to the buyer who then with his escort and the money
will proceed to examine the arms at the place where they are
stored. If on examination the arms are found unsatisfactory
the buyer takes away his money and the deal is off, while
if they are in order half of the arms can be taken delivery
of on the spot.
Fong says he will discuss no other terms and the
question of his prosecution for attempting to deal in arms
may have to be taken into consideration.
Your Obedient Servant,
W Brewster
Detective Sub Inspector.
Murray S. K
Chief Detective Inspector.

表格 2    34
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
864
中央    巡捕房。
1916年11月17日
关于    企图进行武器交易的报告。
由    副巡捕房督察长布鲁斯特制作    转呈者
先生，
    冯焕卿（Fong Wei Ching）再次接受问询，但到目前为止，并未大幅修改其条件。他似乎倾向于达成交易，现在提议，准备购买全部货物的武器买方，如有必要可带20名武装人员护卫，将600,000美元现金带到他家，这是20,000支步枪（每支配备500发子弹）整批货物价格的一半。
    如果他对钞票的真实性感到满意，他将把钞票退还给买方，然后买方在其护卫和资金的陪同下，前往存放地点查验武器。如果查验后发现武器令人不满意，买方带走其资金，交易取消；如果武器符合要求，则可当场提取一半的武器。
    冯表示不再讨论其他条件，且可能需要考虑因其企图进行武器交易而对其提起起诉的问题。
您顺从的仆人，
W 布鲁斯特
副巡捕房督察长。
默里 S. K
总巡捕房督察长。

pages.en:
Shanghai Municipal Police.
（批：8604）

CENTRAL POLICE Station.
14th November 1916.

REPORT ON Attached note re attempted traffic in arms.

Made by D.S.I. Brewster. Forwarded by

Sir,
Fong Wei Ching 馮卿 the person referred to in the attached note lives at 283 Haining Road and is apparently unemployed. He is a Cantonese and was not very long ago employed by the notorious German firm of Schratter & Co. 51B Kiangsi Road, a mushroom concern suspected of dealing in arms and not above suspicion of being engaged in the White Slave Traffic. The firm closed down and the partners absconded leaving many debts behind them.

Fong was interviewed by an agent of the Police who, posing as a middleman, received the usual absurd terms, a copy and translation of which are attached. He wants $60 for each rifle and 50 rounds of ammunition.

It is well known that Fong has no money and I suggest that some Foreigners is at the bottom of the matter.

Your obedient servant,

WB newphew /
Detective Sub-Inspector.

（签名）
Chief Detective Inspector.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
（批注：8604）

中央巡捕房。
1916年11月14日。

关于附注中提及的企图进行武器交易的报告。

由 副巡捕房督察长布鲁斯特制作。转呈者

先生，
    附注中提及的冯卿（Fong Wei Ching）住在海宁路283号，显然无业。他是广东人，不久前受雇于臭名昭著的德国商行施拉特公司（Schratter & Co.），地址江西路51B号，这是一家像蘑菇一样突然冒出的公司，涉嫌从事武器交易，且不排除参与白奴贸易的嫌疑。该公司已关闭，合伙人潜逃，留下许多债务。
    一名伪装成中间人的警务线人对冯进行了问询，收到了通常那种荒谬的条件，其副本及译文附后。他要求每支步枪60美元及50发子弹。
    众所周知，冯没有资金，我建议此事背后有外国人操纵。

您顺从的仆人，

WB newphew /
副巡捕房督察长。

（签名）
总巡捕房督察长。

Translation.

The whole amount of the price of the goods
(when decided) should be deposited in a Japanese
bank in Shanghai in the name of the buyer and seller.
The manager of the said bank should sign a
cheque for half of the amount of the price
and give it to the seller. The latter will
then show the goods to the buyer for examination.
The remaining half of the money should be
paid within 10 days, the amount to be paid
each time should be decided according as the goods
are delivered.
The goods are kept in the Settlement. In the
event of examination the presence of a foreigner
will be necessary.

Pol. No. 7213.
